title: Udta Teer Doubles Over Weekend to Near Rs 19 Crore
excerpt: The Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan spy comedy grew from Rs 3.89 crore on Friday to about Rs 7.9 crore on Sunday - now Monday's hold will decide if it can reach Rs 50 crore.
body:
• Udta Teer, the Hindi-language spy comedy starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan, closed its opening weekend at about Rs 19 crore India net, according to Sacnilk and Bollywood Hungama estimates.
  • The trend is the story: Rs 3.89 crore on Friday, about Rs 7.04 crore on Saturday and about Rs 7.9 crore on Sunday in Bollywood Hungama's early estimates - a doubling from opening day.
  • Sacnilk put the India net at Rs 19.45 crore, with worldwide gross at Rs 27.58 crore including Rs 4.50 crore overseas, across 18,449 shows.
  • Monday's hold will decide whether the film can push toward the Rs 50 crore mark Bollywood Hungama says is now in reach, or fade after a word-of-mouth weekend.

A slow opening turned into a weekend worth watching. Udta Teer, released on October 23, opened at Rs 3.89 crore on Friday, then jumped to Rs 7.04 crore on Saturday and peaked at about Rs 7.9 crore on Sunday, taking its three-day total to Rs 18.83 crore in Bollywood Hungama's early estimates. Sacnilk's tracker put the India net slightly higher, at Rs 19.45 crore, with India gross of Rs 23.08 crore and overseas gross of Rs 4.50 crore for a worldwide gross of Rs 27.58 crore. Tracker estimates differ in timing and method, but both tell the same story: the film roughly doubled from Friday to Sunday.

How the weekend built

Pinkvilla's day-two report captured the turn. After a low opening - its table listed Friday at Rs 3.75 crore, within the range other trackers reported - the film collected Rs 7-7.25 crore nett on Saturday, bringing the two-day total to about Rs 11 crore nett and putting a first weekend of around Rs 19 crore nett in view. Pinkvilla noted the film was outperforming in bigger urban centres, which can limit the Sunday jump comedy films usually get, and that the Saturday growth implied the film had found some acceptance with audiences.

The film behind the numbers

Udta Teer is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language spy comedy directed and written by Aakash Kaushik in his directorial debut, and produced by Karan Johar, Adar Poonawalla, Guneet Monga, Apoorva Mehta and Achin Jain under Dharma Productions and Sikhya Entertainment. Khurrana plays Bilal Ahmad, also known as Vikrant, and Sara Ali Khan plays Yamini, with Rahul Bose, Ram Kapoor, Gulshan Grover, Mukul Dev, Suhail Nayyar, Supriya Pilgaonkar, Brijendra Kala and Sandeep Anand in supporting roles. The film runs 134 minutes, with songs by Sachin-Jigar. It is the second posthumous appearance of Mukul Dev, who died in 2025.

Critical response was mixed to positive. Bollywood Hungama's own review gave the film 3 stars out of 5, calling it an amusing spy comedy that works on its quirky premise and performances, especially Rahul Bose and the late Mukul Dev, while noting it released with minimal hype and would need strong word of mouth. That word of mouth is what the Saturday and Sunday numbers appear to reflect.

Why Monday matters more than Sunday

Weekend growth from a low base is encouraging, but it is not a verdict. Bollywood Hungama argued the film now has a shot at Rs 50 crore, which from a Rs 3.89 crore opening would be a win for the makers, while stressing that weekday holds will decide its fate and that it benefits from a clean run into its second weekend. Pinkvilla made the same point from the other direction: the film needs to consolidate and then hold steady on weekdays, it has one open week, and the arrival of Ramayana: Part One after that will end the clear run. For Khurrana, whose pre-pandemic run of consecutive hits made him a reliable mid-budget draw, Pinkvilla noted the post-pandemic box office has been harsher - a Rs 7-8 crore opening day would have put this film on course for a hit, which is why the recovery since Friday carries weight.

What this means for diaspora audiences

Overseas gross of Rs 4.50 crore in Sacnilk's worldwide tally shows the film is finding viewers outside India as well as at home. For diaspora audiences deciding on a weekday screening, the practical read is the same as the trade's: this is a Hindi-language comedy whose audience grew after opening day, so showtimes are likely to hold through the week if Monday confirms the trend.

What happens next

Monday's collection is the test every report is waiting for. A drop in line with a normal weekday fall keeps the Rs 50 crore path open; a steep fall turns a good weekend into a front-loaded one. Either way, Udta Teer has already done the harder thing - it persuaded more people to buy tickets on Sunday than on the day it opened.
